content_rules.interaction_gate: action-only (the participant must perform the action, never know the answer); never knowledge-gated
content_rules.echo_labels_policy: Any label shown on interaction may only repeat a word the narrator has already said at that moment; nothing new, no extra on-screen text beyond that
content_rules.narration_in_vr: head-locked / non-positional, same original audio track as C1-C3
content_rules.health_claims: No added health claims or advice anywhere in the interface; keep the video's own cautious framing

segments.label: Tradition and Nature
segments.visual: Sanskrit scroll titled Ayurveda; river valley with banyan; sages under the tree with an open book

segments.label: The Five Elements
segments.visual: Open book with element icons dissolving into the diagram: Earth, Fire, Air, Water around a seated figure, cosmos circle on top

segments.label: Plants and Preparations
segments.visual: Herb plants and a hand touching a leaf; hands grinding herbs in a stone mortar; cut to black at ~0:53

segments.label: The Three Doshas
segments.visual: Three medallions: Vata (blue figure with wind/water), Pitta (red figure in flame), Kapha (green figure with leaves)

segments.label: Daily Routines
segments.visual: Figure meditating on a river bank at sunrise; light fades ~1:11

segments.label: Therapies and Preparations
segments.visual: Therapist working on a covered patient on a wooden table; small brass bowl on a stand

segments.label: Texts, Teachers & Continuation
segments.visual: Elder teacher and student reading a manuscript, rolled scrolls and clay pots; river with a flowering plant; young woman standing at the river

pre_survey.prompt: Before today, how much did you already know about Ayurveda?

assessment.title: Ayurveda Study — Post-Experience Questionnaire
assessment.subtitle: Participant copy • Same questionnaire for C1, C2, C3 and C4
assessment.purpose: This questionnaire measures what you remember from the Ayurveda presentation and how clear and engaging you found the experience. There are no questions about whether you personally agree with Ayurveda. Please answer based on the content you experienced.
assessment.instructions: For Q1–Q8, select one answer. Choose “Not sure” if you do not know. For Q9, answer in one or two sentences. For Q10–Q13, circle one number for each statement. Please do not discuss answers with other participants.

levels.label: Part A — What you remember (Q1–Q8)
levels.description: Questions Q1–Q8 measuring recall of presentation content.

items.question: According to the presentation, Ayurveda is a traditional way of understanding…
options: Life, health, and our relationship with nature

items.question: What did the presentation say Ayurvedic traditions observe or reflect on?
options: Nature, everyday rhythms, and connections among body, mind, and environment

items.question: Which five elements were named in the presentation?
options: Earth, water, fire, air, and ether
Earth, metal, wood, ice, and smoke
Water, sand, light, sound, and stone
Fire, rain, cloud, snow, and wind

items.question: What did traditional practitioners do with plants and other natural substances?
options: Studied them and recorded their uses

items.question: Which practices did the presentation say are emphasized in many Ayurvedic traditions?
options: Daily routines, mindful eating, and seasonal practices

items.question: How did the presentation describe therapies and preparations?
options: Intended to support well-being, with practices varying by context

items.question: How was traditional knowledge described as being preserved and passed on?
options: Through traditional texts and from teacher to student across generations

open_response.question: In one or two sentences, what was the main message of the presentation?

experience_survey.prompt: I understood the main message of the presentation.
I paid attention to the presentation for most of the session.
The information was presented in a way that was easy for me to follow.
I can remember at least two important ideas from the presentation.

c4_discomfort.prompt: During the VR experience, how severe was any dizziness, nausea, eye strain, or other discomfort you experienced?
c4_discomfort.instruction: If discomfort was present, please tell the researcher. Follow the study’s approved safety procedure.
